summary: a discovery module: interview, riskiest hypotheses, prototype, architecture handoff and exit gate skills, with a workflow, exit criteria and a Discovery profile
appCreator: Nothing changes in an app until it adds the module (pack add discovery, which also brings the research module). It is meant for a new product idea, before a stack is chosen, and for removal once building starts; the documents it produced stay.

With the module, discovery has a method: one document at a time, by interview (one question at a time, each with a recommended answer): the product foundation, personas checked against research evidence, success metrics, constraints and non-goals, then the MVP and roadmap, written so they turn into the PRD and backlog later.

You can ask for the riskiest hypotheses (ranked, each with a cheap test), for a throwaway clickable prototype that says what it can and cannot prove, for three different design directions after a rejected prototype, and for an architecture handoff that a separate agent on a strong model reviews before you see it.
Asking where discovery stands gives a scored report of nine exit criteria and the next steps. It only reports: building starts when you say "start building".

A short Discovery profile in the app's CLAUDE.md holds the product facts the skills read, and your sign-off mode: approve each document (the default), or let documents merge on their own with a record you can ask a recap of.
The handoff review costs one agent run on a strong model at high effort.

The routing test ran once over 77 queries on Sonnet (70 right; 14 of the 16 new ones; no request was sent to a wrong discovery skill; the misses are requests where the model looked at files before picking a skill, one of them an exit-gate request). Trial runs led to wording fixes in the skills; the fixed wording was not trial-run again.
